'''Marjorie Violet Mussett''' (1922 - 21 December 2004) was a British biologist and [[endocrinology|endocrinologist]].

==Career==
She obtained a Bachelor of Science degree from the [[University of London]] in 1950.<ref>{{cite book|title=Directory of British Scientists|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2aq4AAAAIAAJ|accessdate=26 July 2013|year=1966|publisher=E. Benn Limited}}</ref>

She worked at the [[National Institute for Medical Research]] from 1951 to 1974, in Biological Standards and Statistical Services, and transferred to the [[National Institute for Biological Standards and Control]] when this was separated. Marjorie worked as a statistician and was recognised for her contribution to the statistical reliability, with many acknowledgements of her work.<ref>{{cite book|last1=MRC National Institute for Medical Research|title=A century of science for health|date=2014|publisher=MRC National Institute for Medical Research|location=London|chapter-url=http://www.historyofnimr.org.uk/files/2014/07/chapter14.pdf|chapter=14}}</ref>

She authored [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/?term=Mussett+MV 48 papers], mainly on the creation of international standards for [[antibiotics]]. 

At the time of her death, she was living in Blenheim Road, Harrow, Middlesex.{{Citation needed|date=November 2014}}
